nodes_add.name: Krishna Prem (Ronald Nixon)
nodes_add.note: Born Cheltenham 10 May 1898; RFC pilot; Lucknow 1921; initiated by Yashoda Ma 1928; Mirtola ashram near Almora from 1929; head 1944; d. Mirtola 14 Nov 1965.

nodes_add.name: Sri Yashoda Ma (Monica Devi Chakravarti)
nodes_add.note: Born Monica Roy 1882; wife of Gyanendra Nath Chakravarti; took renunciant vows 1928; initiated Krishna Prem; co-founded Mirtola; d. 1944.

nodes_add.name: Madhava Ashish (Alexander Phipps)
nodes_add.note: Born Edinburgh 23 Feb 1920; RAF engineer; visited Ramana 1944; at Mirtola after the war; head of the ashram 1965-1997; Padma Shri 1992; d. 13 April 1997. Succeeded by his disciple Dev Ashish.

edges_upsert.note: She took vairagya vows in 1928 as Yashoda Mai and initiated Nixon, who took the name Krishna Prem.
Mentor and successor as head of Mirtola in 1965.
A 1944 holiday visit to Ramana's ashram began his spiritual search (Wikipedia).

Yashoda Ma was initiated by Bal Krishna Goswami of the Radha Raman temple, Brindaban (Quest); Haberman calls him perhaps the first Westerner on the path of Krishna-bhakti and Sardella the first European to embrace Vaishnavism in India (cited on Wikipedia).

Quest article (self-described anecdotal) mentions his first draft of a commentary on the Stanzas of Dzyan; Man, the Measure of All Things in the Stanzas of Dzyan (1969, with Madhava Ashish) is documented on Wikipedia.

krishna-prem.mdx: Wikipedia's claim that he was the first Westerner in Gaudiya Vaishnavism is a scholars' assertion not checked against a scholarly source.
